title: The Minority Attack
subtitle: Advance two pawns against three — and leave a weakness behind.
goals: Push b4–b5 to create a backward c-pawn
Defend by counterattacking in the centre

steps.say: This looks upside down: White attacks on the queenside where Black has MORE pawns. That is exactly the point. By pushing b2–b4–b5 into a three-pawn majority, White forces an exchange that leaves Black with a permanently backward pawn on c6 — a weakness on an open file that lasts the rest of the game. The minority attack is the clearest example in chess of playing for a structural target rather than a tactic.

steps.prompt: Launch the minority attack — send the b-pawn on its way!
hints: Two pawns are marching at three. The goal is not to win material but to force a weakness on c6.
b4, heading for b5 where it hits the c6 pawn.

line.say: The march begins. Next comes b5, and when Black captures (or allows bxc6), his c-pawn becomes backward on a half-open file — a target his pieces must babysit for the rest of the game. Two pawns advancing into three: the arithmetic looks wrong and the strategy is perfect.

rejections.say: A useful preparatory move in some versions, but slow — Black gets time for ...a5 stopping the whole plan. When the minority attack is available, play b4 immediately.
Opening the centre helps the defender: with the centre open, Black's pieces come alive and your queenside plan becomes irrelevant. Minority attacks require a stable centre.

steps.wrongSay: Push the pawn that will attack c6 — the b-pawn.
steps.successSay: The target is c6, and the weapon is a pawn that will be exchanged, not queened.

steps.prompt: The pawn has reached b4 and Black met it with ...a6. Continue the plan!
hints: Don't be distracted: the plan is to reach b5 and force the exchange on c6.
b5! Whether Black takes or allows bxc6, the c-pawn becomes backward.

line.say: The critical moment. Now ...axb5 cxb5 leaves Black's c6 pawn backward on the half-open c-file, or ...cxb5 cxb5 gives you a protected passer and the c-file. Either way, the structural damage is permanent — and permanent is what strategy means.

rejections.say: Supporting the push looks natural but wastes time and lets Black organize ...c5. The pawn should arrive at b5 while Black is still untangling.
Piece play instead of the pawn push. The minority attack is carried out by PAWNS; the pieces only support the resulting weakness afterwards.

steps.wrongSay: Continue the march: the b-pawn goes to b5 and forces the exchange.
steps.successSay: One pawn push, one permanent weakness. That is a plan you can play for twenty moves.

steps.say: And the defence, since you will be on both sides: meet a minority attack with counterplay in the CENTRE or on the kingside, where you have the extra pawn. Trading pieces does not help the defender here — activity does. If you're ever the one with a backward c-pawn, your plan is ...c5 (breaking the structure) or a kingside attack. Structure against activity is the oldest argument in chess.
